questions.question: What is the lesson's core invariant for using an indicator?
options: Every imported indicator should become a permanent block rule.
An indicator is a time-bounded claim with context, not an instruction by itself.
A TAXII collection proves every object inside it is correct.
More feeds always produce better intelligence.
questions.explanation: A platform must preserve provenance, confidence, validity, markings, and intended use. The downstream action needs its own policy gate.

questions.question: The phishing-domain candidate starts at confidence 86 and loses 8 points every 7 days. What is its effective confidence at age 17 days?
questions.explanation: Seventeen days contains two complete seven-day decay periods, so the model calculates 86 - (2 x 8) = 70.

questions.question: Why should the shared-hosting IP remain out of automated prevention even though it has many sightings?
options: IP addresses cannot be represented in threat intelligence.
Its high false-positive risk means blocking it could affect unrelated tenants and legitimate services.
Sightings are valid only for file hashes.
Automated prevention requires exactly one sighting.
questions.explanation: Sightings add evidence, but they do not erase shared-infrastructure risk. Action policy must account for likely collateral impact.

questions.question: Which statement correctly separates STIX 2.1 from TAXII 2.1?
options: STIX models CTI objects and relationships; TAXII exposes services and collections for exchanging CTI objects.
STIX is an HTTPS authentication scheme; TAXII is a confidence score.
STIX replaces sharing policy; TAXII replaces analyst review.
They are two names for the same JSON file.
questions.explanation: STIX is the representation language. TAXII defines application-layer APIs for discovery, collections, manifests, objects, and status.

questions.question: A source wants TLP:AMBER information restricted to the recipient's organization and not its clients. Which TLP 2.0 marking expresses that boundary?
options: TLP:CLEAR
TLP:GREEN
TLP:AMBER+STRICT
TLP:RED shared through a public collection
questions.explanation: FIRST TLP 2.0 defines TLP:AMBER+STRICT for organization-only sharing. Ordinary TLP:AMBER also permits need-to-know sharing with clients.

questions.question: What is the operational consequence when consumer feedback never returns to the TIP?
options: Normalization automatically becomes more accurate.
The platform cannot learn from sightings, false positives, dispositions, or disablement outcomes.
TAXII converts all indicators into reports.
The source marking becomes TLP:CLEAR.
questions.explanation: Without a feedback path, confidence and expiry decisions cannot reflect real consumer outcomes, so stale or noisy intelligence can persist.

questions.question: Which metric best reveals whether a feed produces usable intelligence rather than merely high volume?
options: Raw objects ingested per day by itself
Number of vendor logos on the integration page
Actionable yield with released and accepted counts, followed by false-positive outcomes
Total storage allocated to the platform
questions.explanation: Actionable yield keeps the denominator visible and becomes meaningful when paired with later false-positive and disposition feedback.
